title: A uniform principal localization lifts coordinate idempotents
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings with B an A-algebra. Let K be a field with an A-algebra structure, K' a field with compatible K- and A-algebra structures, r a natural number, and L_j fields with K'-algebra structures for j in Fin(r). Fix a K'-algebra equivalence e from the quotient of (K tensor_A B) tensor_K K' by its nilradical onto the product of the L_j. Here the nilradical is the ideal of nilpotent elements. Assume K is a fraction field of A. Let R0 be a domain with compatible maps A to R0 to K' making K' a fraction field of R0. There exists nonzero t in R0 such that, for every s divisible by t and every principal localization R=R0[1/s] in the universe of A, with compatible maps A to R0 to R to K' and K' a fraction field of R, and every compatible R-algebra structure on the L_j, every compatible R-algebra homomorphism f from (B tensor_A R) modulo its nilradical to the product of the L_j contains each coordinate vector: for every j there exists x in its source such that f(x)_i is 1 for i=j and 0 otherwise. Call f compatible when for every b in B its value on the class of b tensor 1 is e of the class of (1 tensor b) tensor 1. No finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

proof.text: The images g(b) of the pure tensors ((1 tensor b) tensor 1) span the product over K'. To check this, lift an arbitrary vector through e inverse and Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective. Induct on the outer tensor and then on its inner tensor. For a pure tensor ((k tensor b) tensor c), its image is (c times the image of k) times g(b); zero and addition preserve span membership.

For any subset S in a K'-vector space and any vector in its K'-span, find a nonzero R0 scalar that moves it into the R0-span. Prove this by Submodule.span_induction: generators and zero use denominator 1; sums use the product of the two denominators; for scalar multiplication write the scalar as n/q using IsFractionRing.div_surjective and multiply the previous denominator by q. Apply this to each coordinate vector z_j and choose its denominator d_j.

Take t to be the finite product of d_j. The product is nonzero by Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff. If t divides s, then d_j divides s by Finset.dvd_prod_of_mem; IsLocalization.Away.isUnit_of_dvd makes its image in R a unit. This also covers r=0, when the product is 1 and there is no coordinate assertion.

For any compatible f, restrict its linear map to R0. Compatibility puts each g(b) in its range, so Submodule.span_le puts the entire R0-span of these generators in its range. Thus d_j times z_j equals f(x) for some x. Choose the unit u in R representing d_j and multiply x by u inverse. R-linearity and the scalar-tower identities give f(u inverse times x)=z_j. Evaluating at each coordinate proves the assertion.

theorem exists_generic_product_idempotent_bound
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (B : Type v) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (K' : Type (max u v)) [Field K'] [Algebra K K'] [Algebra A K']
    [IsScalarTower A K K']
    (R0 : Type (max u v)) [CommRing R0] [IsDomain R0]
    [Algebra A R0] [Algebra R0 K'] [IsScalarTower A R0 K']
    [IsFractionRing R0 K']
    (r : ℕ) (L : Fin r → Type (max u v)) [∀ j, Field (L j)]
    [∀ j, Algebra K' (L j)]
    (e :
      letI := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (R := K) (A := K ⊗[A] B) (B := K')
      (((K ⊗[A] B) ⊗[K] K') ⧸
        nilradical ((K ⊗[A] B) ⊗[K] K')) ≃ₐ[K'] (∀ j, L j))
    : ∃ t : R0, t ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ s : R0, t ∣ s →
      ∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra R0 R] [IsLocalization.Away s R]
        [Algebra A R] [IsScalarTower A R0 R] [Algebra R K']
        [IsScalarTower R0 R K'] [IsFractionRing R K']
        [∀ j, Algebra R (L j)] [∀ j, IsScalarTower R K' (L j)],
        letI := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (R := A) (A := B) (B := R)
        ∀ f : ((B ⊗[A] R) ⧸ nilradical (B ⊗[A] R)) →ₐ[R] (∀ j, L j),
            (∀ b : B, f (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (b ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : R))) =
              e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[A] b) ⊗ₜ[K] (1 : K')))) →
          (∀ j, ∃ x, ∀ i, f x i = if i = j then 1 else 0)
